title: Out-of-State Owners
metaTitle: Selling Arkansas Mineral Rights as an Out-of-State Owner
metaDescription: Live outside Arkansas but own Smackover or Fayetteville mineral rights? We handle the whole process remotely, from valuation to closing paperwork.
heroLead: Owning minerals two states, or a country, away from the property means every question about the lease, the well, or the check takes longer to answer than it should.
intro: A large share of Arkansas mineral owners we work with don't live in Arkansas. The interest came through a grandparent's estate, or a job transfer decades ago left family land behind, or the tract was simply always owned from a distance. Managing that from another state means you're dependent on operator mailings for information, you can't easily drive to the county clerk's office to pull a record, and any dispute over a division order or a missed payment takes longer to resolve because you're not local.

We built our process around exactly that gap. Everything from the initial valuation to the closing documents can be handled remotely, by phone, email, and mail, without you needing to set foot in Arkansas. We do the county-level legwork ourselves.

sections.heading: What We Handle So You Don't Have To
paragraphs: Pulling deed and probate records at the county clerk's office, checking current Oil and Gas Commission unit and permit filings, and verifying operator and division-order information are all things we do on our end using the county, section, and legal description you provide. You don't need to track down courthouse records yourself or interpret an operator's pooling notice to know what it means for your interest.

If your ownership traces through a chain of title that's unclear from where you're sitting, an out-of-state probate, a name change, a deed that was never properly recorded, we'll tell you specifically what's missing and, where we can, help identify how to resolve it rather than leaving you to figure out Arkansas title requirements from a different state's legal framework.

sections.heading: Closing Without a Trip to Arkansas
paragraphs: Mineral deed transfers don't require an in-person closing. Documents can be prepared, reviewed, and signed remotely, with notarization handled through a local notary wherever you live, and the recorded deed and payment sent by mail or wire. We walk you through exactly what each document does before you sign anything, since a mineral deed is a permanent transfer and we want you to understand it, not only sign where indicated.
For owners overseas, the same process works, it just takes a bit longer for document transit and notarization logistics, and we plan the timeline around that rather than rushing it.

sections.heading: Why Distance Makes Selling More Appealing for Some Owners
paragraphs: An absentee owner is more exposed to a few specific risks: missing a lease ratification deadline because mail got delayed or forwarded incorrectly, not noticing a division order error until months of underpayment have accumulated, or being unreachable when an operator needs a signature to keep a well in a favorable pooling configuration. None of that is a reason you have to sell, but it's a real, ongoing cost of managing minerals from a distance that some owners decide isn't worth continuing to carry, especially for a modest interest that doesn't justify the attention it demands.

sections.heading: Verifying Who You're Dealing With
paragraphs: Out-of-state owners are also more frequently targeted by low, pressure-tactic mailer offers from buyers betting that distance makes owners less likely to check comparable offers or verify the buyer. We encourage you to check any offer, including ours, against production or lease data before signing, and we're glad to explain exactly how we arrived at our number rather than asking you to take it on faith.

sections.heading: Coordinating Across Time Zones and Multiple Heirs
paragraphs: It's common for an out-of-state family to have heirs spread across three or four states, each holding a fractional share of the same original interest, and none of them coordinating with each other on what to do. We can work with each heir individually on their own share and timeline rather than requiring the whole family to agree and act in lockstep, which is often the practical difference between a sale that actually closes and one that stalls indefinitely waiting for consensus that never arrives.

faqs.question: Do I need to travel to Arkansas to sell my mineral rights?
faqs.answer: No. The entire process, valuation, document review, signing, and notarization, can be completed remotely from wherever you live, with documents sent by mail or electronically and notarized locally.

faqs.question: I've lost track of my exact legal description and deed. Can you still help?
faqs.answer: Yes, we can pull county deed and probate records ourselves using your name, the county, and approximate property information to reconstruct the chain of title.

faqs.question: How do I know I'm not being lowballed since I can't check comps myself?
faqs.answer: We'll explain the production or lease data behind our offer directly, and you're welcome to compare it against any other offer you've received before deciding. We'd rather earn the sale on a transparent number than a rushed one.

faqs.question: I live overseas. Does that complicate the transfer?
faqs.answer: It adds some time for document transit and notarization logistics, but the process itself is the same. We'll build a realistic timeline around your location rather than assuming a domestic-speed close.

faqs.question: What if I've been getting mailer offers and don't know which ones are legitimate?
faqs.answer: Verify any buyer's identity and check their offer against your actual production or lease data before signing anything. We're happy to walk through how our number was built so you have something concrete to compare against.
